M (puddle water tones, 590 stones with faces, 34 ruts, clods)

blender_tools_used: Cycles (CPU, orthographic top-down camera, box filter 1.0, 8 samples)
Mesh from corner lists (from_pydata) with FACE attributes (colour, brightness, roughness)
Emission shader + Attribute node (exact flat colours)
Curve objects with bevel depth (ruts, geometry route)
Geometry Nodes: Mesh to Points, Instance on Points, Random Value, Noise Texture, Set Position, Set Shade Smooth, Realize Instances, Set Material (stones, geometry route)
Sun lamp + Diffuse BSDF + World colour (geometry-route stones)
numpy after the render: height from colour (stretch 20..128, blur 0.5), normal from 8-bit height (strength 9), cheap AO
changes_wanted_in_lib: A shared flat-shape painter in lib/contrib (build_tile_mesh, channel_material, derive_normal_from_height): the wood and mud generators are about 90 per cent the same code
Move merge_trace.py / trace_tools.py (now in recipes/wood/analysis) and the colour-axis element finder (recipes/mud/analysis/element_tools.py) into lib/contrib
description_audit.py: also print the number of polygon corners (a fairer size measure than JSON bytes)

texture_compare.py: colour_gradient and normal_tilt are 0 unless fine-edge density matches almost exactly (soften); the seam measure reads 2.0-2.5 for anything traced from a reference with its own mild seam; the tiling group is 0 for a crop of a bigger picture
pixel_compare.py: option to ignore a band of N dots at the edge; say in the report when a tier skipped measures because the reference has no maps (mud_golden)
dead_ends: Sorting stones and water by palette colour failed (a stone's lit face is blue-grey like water, pale stones are tan like earth): replaced by a Lab b < 7 pixel test + hole fill + shape tests + watershed
Watershed marker bug (added 1 to every dot so nothing was undecided: every stone one dot big, '0 stones found')
Thin groove lines at scale 3 found only fragments (25 curves); broad rut paths appear at scale 10
Stone clusters first called puddles; fixed by requiring at least 40 per cent clearly blue dots
Smooth ground tone fields buy colour difference but no SSIM (0.49 until the blur is under 3 dots); invented clods lower dot-for-dot scores and make the normal worse than flat (28 vs 23.5 degrees)

Lower normal strengths did not help (19.3 vs 19.9 degrees); tier 'close' unreachable at 512 KB because normal angle stays about 18.6 (palette-snapped 16 colours reach 9.8 only with a per-dot label map)
Geometry Nodes stones: attribute named 'radius' overwritten by Mesh to Points, Vector Math Scale socket mistake, then smooth low-contrast round lumps that do not match the painted look
First sampled puddles amoeba-like, ruts spaghetti with square ends, sampler needs OpenCV (not in Blender): sampling and baking are two steps
False alarm in my own seam test (compared bakes from two code versions); area quarters scored low only because the tiling group is 0 for a crop; I first wrongly blamed a distance grid (fixed anyway)
Own-script mistakes: golden score files overwrote mud's (same names); pkill -f with text from my own command killed my shell
Pebble clusters around big stones did not change the kind score (cannot see it) though they look closer by eye
derivation_ceiling: Height = (0.299R+0.587G+0.114B - 20)/108 cut to 0..1, blurred 0.5 dot: mean error 3.32 levels (correlation 0.997); normal = central slope of the 8-bit height x 9: 0.35 degrees from the uploaded height; from colour-derived height 3.7 degrees (smoother filter, strength 10) or 4.8 (plain, strength 8); flat normal would be 23.5 degrees off. Palette-only ceiling (16 colours snapped, no description): SSIM 0.916, delta E 3.29, edge skill 0.854, height 8.9, normal 9.8 degrees (tier close); a 3x3 median clean-up drops it to SSIM 0.82 / 13.4 degrees.
geometry_route_verdict: Tried in Blender on the M description (590 stones, 34 ruts). Stones by Geometry Nodes (Mesh to Points + Instance on Points + noise Set Position + sun-lit flat shading): 8.4 s vs 3.4 s for flat polygons; needs only 3 numbers per stone and gets lit/shaded faces free, but came out as smooth, low-contrast round lumps without the painted dark rim, so the flat-polygon painter stays the default. Ruts as Blender curve objects (bevel): 3.2 s vs 4.6 s, equal picture but one width/colour per curve (3 curves per rut) and no easy wobble/fade. Height from geometry (hybrid) not tested because the reference height is derived from colour.
variation_result: 8 new tiles from sample_description(seed 101-108) baked at 1254 with the same generator (final sampler: 36,000 smaller clods, pebble clusters): same-kind score mean 0.383 (0.353-0.416; reference-fitted L class 0.483, M 0.362, S 0.267, another surface about 0.1); SSIM against the reference only 0.283 (max 0.288) so none is a copy; SSIM between tiles mean 0.343 (max 0.352, 28 pairs), mean colour difference between tiles 28 levels; seam ratio 0.86-1.18; bake 33-54 s. By eye same family (ruts with banks, ragged puddles, dark angular stones, crumbly ground) but flatter and sparser than the reference: ruts read as scratches rather than flowing bands. Contact sheet: variations/contact_sheet.png.
area_result: One description for 2508 x 2508 dots (sample_description(201, tile=2508), 4x the content, wrapped at 2508), baked at 2508 in 228 s with 114,875 shapes: seam ratio across the wrap edges 0.876 (left/right) and 1.044 (top/bottom) (1.0 = invisible); strongest repeat in the picture's own correlation at 40+ dots 0.176 (ordinary correlation length, not a repeat); the four quarters differ from each other (pairwise SSIM 0.34-0.35). Quarter overall kind scores 0.29-0.31 are low only because a crop is not a wrapping tile (tiling group 0); their colour/height/normal groups match the 1254 tiles. Pictures: guide_pictures/area_2508_small.png and area_seam_closeup.png.
resolution_result: Same description (seed 101) at 512 / 1254 / 2508 dots: bake 15.4 s / 33.3 s / 77.8 s (colour render 3.8 / 10.7 / 27.2 s, 28,757 shapes at every size; shared CPU, times vary ~30 per cent); content identical: SSIM to the 2508 bake shrunk to the same size 0.987 / 0.993 / 1.0. A bigger bake only gives finer anti-aliasing of the same shapes; no extra detail below the description's dot size. Half-tile seam test: sampled tile 0.757 mean levels difference (0.98 per cent of dots over 8 levels); M 0.652 (0.74 per cent); L final 0.793 (1.09 per cent); spread evenly, no seam line.
transfer_result: (1) Snowy track, a surface nobody gave me: same generator and sampler, only a new 16-colour palette, naming which palette entries play band/groove/bank/wet/water, stone_scale 0.35, puddle_scale 0.7, clod_count 9000, zone_weight 0.85 and height stretch 60..245 (one small new sampler option, 'maps'); about ten minutes of work, description in 0.6 s, bake about 40 s; judged by eye only: reads as compacted snow with grey slush tracks, white banks, blue meltwater, dark rocks; weak: rut ends fade like claws, clods too small. (2) mud_golden re-fit (colour only) with the same analysis chain and generator, one number changed (non-earth threshold 3 instead of 7), about 6 minutes of computer time: S 7.1 KB SSIM 0.272 / kind 0.366; M 59.9 KB SSIM 0.312 / kind 0.425; L final 513.7 KB SSIM 0.604, delta E 6.84, edge skill 0.60, kind 0.503 (tier close on colour measures only). Pictures: guide_pictures/transfer_snow.png and transfer_golden.png.
what_each_layer_bought: Flat ground (0.4 KB): SSIM 0.443, delta E 14.2, kind 0.11
+ 8 puddle outlines (3.2 KB) and + 40 big stones (7.1 KB): delta E 14.2 -> 11.0, edge skill 0 -> 0.03, SSIM unchanged (0.45)

S class, ruts + 14,000 invented clods in 7.4 KB: looks like mud (kind 0.267) but SSIM 0.367 and normal 28 degrees (worse than flat 23.5): invented ground lowers dot-for-dot scores, raises the kind score
M class (63.9 KB, water tones + 590 stones with faces): delta E 9.75, edge skill 0.19, kind 0.362, SSIM 0.403
Traced ground 2000 patches (299.5 KB): SSIM 0.633, edge skill 0.564, normal 20.4; 5000 patches (453.4 KB): SSIM 0.688, edge 0.644, normal 18.6
Correction layer painted last (503 KB): SSIM 0.698, delta E 5.0, edge skill 0.685, height 17.6, kind 0.483: cheapest accuracy per byte (+0.03 SSIM for +50 KB vs +0.055 for +154 KB of ground patches)
Blur ladder: smooth ground tone fields buy delta E (8.3 -> 7.7) but no SSIM (0.49) until the 1-3 dot detail is right (0.80 unblurred); the normal angle lives in that same fine detail
lessons_that_transfer: Prove how the maps were made first (10 min): height and normal follow the colour, so the colour picture is the whole problem; then measure two ceilings (palette-snapped copy, and a blur ladder of the ground) to learn which layers can ever buy dot accuracy

Find the 'things' by a one-number colour axis test (Lab b below a threshold calibrated so about a third of the picture is 'not earth'), never by palette entries; then split by shape (size after opening, solidity, share of clearly blue dots) and watershed touching round things
Few big things first (8 puddles), many small things second (830 stones); follow line networks as ridges at the scale where they are valleys (3 dots fragments, 10 dots the rut paths)
Describe the rest as chance tables relative to the structure found (ground colour by distance to the nearest rut and side) plus size/shape/direction numbers; the sampler draws from them with a seed

Build the generator as a painter of flat shapes back to front photographed from above, with wrap copies for seamlessness; make height and normal from the finished colour; keep a numpy preview painter and compare it once with the real bake (0.75 levels)

Invented texture and traced patches must not be mixed in one tile: statistics for new tiles (kind score), tracing for this tile (pixel score); spend the last bytes on a correction layer traced only where the picture is still wrong
Calibrate sampler counts on cheap facts before baking (share non-earth 31%, share dark, density of fine edges) and look at the pictures: the kind tool cannot see clusters
Re-bake every row after a generator fix and compare only bakes from the same code; score a crop of a big picture by its parts, not the overall number; keep outputs in separate folders per surface
Transfer by changing numbers only (palette, which entries play which role, counts, analysis threshold, height stretch); mud to snow took ten minutes, mud to golden mud one threshold number
known_gaps: Tier 'close' not reached for the mud: normal angle 18.6 degrees against the 12 limit (best palette-snapped label map reaches 9.8 but cannot be described in 512 KB); best class is 'layout' at 503 KB
The L class is tracing the picture (about 61,000 traced corners + 830 stones, 163,631 numbers), not procedural description; invented ground and traced patches are never mixed
Stones are cut into pieces by the watershed (big stones look chopped, each piece with its own base colour); tan/orange stones are only traced

Sampled tiles are flatter and sparser than the reference: ruts read as scratches not flowing S-bands with lit crests; pebble-cluster rule is a guess not a fit; kind score 0.38 on average, fine-edge density (colour_gradient) still the weakest measure
Reference-fitted S and M rows use the first 14,000 clods; the sampler's later default (36,000 smaller clods) was not applied to them

Geometry Nodes stones did not match the painted look (stronger sun / sharper shapes / dark rim not tried); hybrid height from real geometry, Dynamic Paint/particles for ruts, EEVEE, compositor stylising and a 4x4 area were not tested
Roughness (0.97 - 0.55 x brightness), metallic (0) and AO maps have no reference and were not checked; water is not made glossy

Snow transfer judged by eye only (rut ends like claws, clods too small); golden L description is 513.7 KB (inside 512 KiB, over 512,000 bytes); golden has no height/normal reference so its tier uses colour measures only; kind score noise is +-0.03-0.05
